# GMD-15 — Banque N1 (formative, M1→M4)

```
Sourced against GMD-25's own repo-truth (cited, never re-derived) and
standard live-events safety/access-management practice.
```

## M1 — 3 real scan outcomes

1. Name the 3 real scan outcomes per GMD-25's worked example, and one
   correct operator action per outcome. (Valid — admit; duplicate —
   deny, flag; invalid — deny, escalate if pattern repeats)

## M2 — live counter literacy

2. What does `GET /scan/counter/{eid}` count, per GMD-25's repo-truth?
   (Live attendance based on valid scans for that event — cited, not
   re-derived)

## M3 — escalation boundary discipline

3. What must an operator do when a scan failure is not one of the 3
   known outcomes? (Escalate to a human immediately — never invent a
   workaround, per GMD-25/GMD-34's own declared gap: no automated
   incident/recovery path exists)
4. Why is this boundary explicitly documented rather than filled with
   an invented recovery procedure? (Because GMD-34 — Incident &
   Recovery Operations — is itself a declared, unbuilt gap; inventing
   a procedure here would fabricate a capability the real platform
   does not have)

## M4 — market-general safety protocols beyond the platform

5. Name two standard event-safety practices not represented in the
   real platform's code at all. (Crowd-density monitoring, medical/
   emergency-services coordination)
6. How must such practices be labeled when taught here? (Explicitly
   `NOT_A_PLATFORM_CAPABILITY` — legitimate industry protocol
   knowledge, never presented as a Good Mood platform feature)
